About Me

My name is Amos Kipngeno, born on June 24, 2001 in the picturesque town of Molo, Nakuru County. As the fifth-born in my family, my early years were shaped by the warm embrace of my parents and a close-knit community that placed education and hard work at the heart of everything.

From Kogo Junior Primary School — where I excelled in Science and Kiswahili, served as class captain, joined the choir, debating team, and environmental club — to Molo Academy Boys High School where I pursued the science stream and earned a Certificate of Merit in KCSE 2021, every chapter has been defined by perseverance and growth.

Now in my final year at Dedan Kimathi University of Technology, I have developed real-world digital solutions including an Electronic Queue Management System that cut medical centre wait times by 60%. My skills span the full web stack — HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP, Node.js, MySQL — and I am passionate about using technology to solve African problems and build a sustainable digital future for Kenya.

Video Presentations

30 Marks · 3 × 10

Three 20-minute video presentations. Press play to watch directly on this page, or click YouTube to open in a new tab.

Innovation / Invention · 10 Marks
Electronic Queue Management System for School Medical Centre
A web-based solution that reduced medical centre wait times from 75 to 28 minutes (60% improvement) and raised student satisfaction from 3.2 to 8.5 out of 10. Built with PHP, MySQL, QR code check-in, real-time dashboard, and SMS notifications.
▶ YouTube
African Culture & Gender Awareness · 10 Marks
Ubuntu Philosophy: African Communal Values in Modern Technology
"I am because we are." An exploration of Ubuntu's five core principles, its gender awareness dimensions — strengths and patriarchal challenges — and practical applications in modern technology: M-Pesa, open-source development, and community networks.
▶ YouTube
Modern Society Challenge · 10 Marks
Cybersecurity Threats: Protecting Our Digital Future
Kenya suffered 40 million cyberattacks in 2024, costing Ksh 40 billion annually. A comprehensive 5-pillar national cybersecurity solution framework, with a vision for Kenya as East Africa's cybersecurity hub by 2030.
▶ YouTube

Photographic Essay

10 Marks

Climate Change & Environmental Crisis in Africa

Africa faces record droughts, catastrophic floods, and devastating heatwaves intensified by climate change. This essay documents the human cost across Malawi, Zimbabwe, Nigeria, Tanzania, and Kenya.

🏜️
Drought & Water Scarcity
Parched farmland in Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe where crop harvests dropped 40–50%. Families queue at scarce wells as water sources dry up.
🌊
Flooding & Displacement
Catastrophic floods in Nigeria killed hundreds and displaced over 1.3 million people. Families forced into makeshift shelters.
🌱
Land Degradation
Severe land degradation in rural Tanzania forces farmers into poverty, destroying agricultural livelihoods.
🦗
Desert Locust Invasions
Climate-intensified locust swarms destroy entire crop seasons, threatening food security for 25 million people across East Africa.
👨‍🌾
Impact on Rural Communities
Rural farmers in Mathari face economic devastation as climate shocks and lack of infrastructure destroy incomes.
💡
Call to Action
Integrated water management, sustainable land-use, and African-led environmental solutions are urgently needed.
